o: The apostle commends Gaius for piety and hospitality.
Cautions him against siding with Diotrephes, who was a turbulent spirit; but recommends Demetrius as a man of excellent character.
He hopes soon to see Gaius.
bg: Is addressed to Caius, or Gaius, but whether to the Christian of that name in Macedonia (Acts 19: 29) or in Corinth (Rom. 16:23) or in Derbe (Acts 20:4) is uncertain. It was written for the purpose of commending to Gaius some Christians who were strangers in the place where he lived, and who had gone thither for the purpose of preaching the gospel (ver. 7).
A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle (3 John 1:1).
Jove-nourished, rebuked by John for his pride (3 John 1:9). He was a Judaizer, prating against John and his fellow-labourers "with malicious words" (7).
A Christian who is spoken of as having "a good report of all men, and of the truth itself" (3 John 1:12).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle commends Gaius for piety and hospitality (vv. 1–8); Cautions him against siding with Diotrephes, who was a turbulent spirit; but recommends Demetrius as a man of excellent character (vv. 9–12); He hopes soon to see Gaius (vv. 13,14). People named: Gaius, Diotrephes, Demetrius.
ch.mh: Those who are beloved of Christ, will love the brethren for his sake.
q: Read verses 1–8 (The apostle commends Gaius for piety and hospitality). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 9–12 (Cautions him against siding with Diotrephes, who was a turbulent spirit; but recommends Demetrius as a man of excellent character), what do you learn about the church and fellowship?
Verse 11 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Isaiah 1:16–17. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Gaius’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of truth and light in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 3 John?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: We must be ready to bear our testimony to them; and it is well when those who commend, can appeal to the consciences of such as know most of those who are commended.
ch.a: Do one concrete, unannounced act of love for someone in your home or church.
